title: Print a blank form in another of its languages

items.text: If a form has been translated, for example into Filipino, “Print blank” on the form’s page now asks which language to print in. The scanner reads only the form’s main language, so a copy printed in another language says at the bottom that its answers must be typed in by hand.

title: A short answer on a scan is no longer mistaken for printed text

items.text: When a filled paper copy is scanned, a one-word answer that happens to appear in the form’s printed text, such as “FORM” written above the line that says “Scans of this form…”, is now read as the answer. Before, it was skipped as printed text and the question showed as blank.

title: Changing a date question to a time warns you first

items.text: When you change a question from a date to a time, or from a time to a date or a date and time, the builder now warns you about each condition or rule that compares it with a date or a time, because those comparisons would stop working and the form could not be published until you fix them. Changing a date to a date and time still works without a warning.

title: Rules say when “contains” matches text

items.text: In the builder, a rule that compares a single-choice or dropdown question now calls “contains” “contains the text”. It checks the letters of the chosen answer, so “contains re” holds for both Red and Green. Rules you already made work exactly as before.

title: Moving a section says which one

items.text: With a screen reader, moving a section in the builder’s Structure view now says the section’s name when you pick it up, move it and drop it, as moving a question already did. Before, it said only “a section”.

title: Rename a section where you see it

items.text: In the builder’s Structure view, a section’s title can now be edited on the section itself, as a question’s label already can: press the pencil beside it, or double-click it. Enter saves, and Escape keeps the old title.
A section you have just added can now be saved straight away. Before, any change to it showed Not saved, with a message about whether it repeats, until you reloaded the page.

title: Saved questions keep their rules as loose as they were

items.text: When you use Save to library on a question whose rules are grouped (any of these, or all of these) and one rule in the group compares with another question, the whole group is now left out of the saved copy. Before, only the comparison was left out, so the copy was stricter than the question you saved. A comparison with another question still cannot be saved to the library, because the other question is not there.

title: XLSForm imports with long appearances

items.text: Importing an XLSForm no longer fails when a question’s appearance is longer than 60 characters, such as an ODK search() lookup. The question is imported without that appearance, and the import’s warnings say which question it was.

title: XLSForm exports keep translated choices

items.text: A form translated only in its answer choices, or in the rows and columns of a grid, now keeps those translations when you export it to XLSForm. Before, the export left them out unless a question's own label was translated too.

title: Builder panels that grow with your text

items.text: With Text size set to Large or Extra large (Settings → Appearance), the builder’s left panel (Add) and right panel (Settings) now widen with the text, so they keep the same room for their words as at the standard size. The form in the middle gives up that width. At the standard text size nothing changes.

title: BHW Connect, one click away

items.text: BHW Connect, the Barangay Health Worker dashboard on this same site, is now linked from your account menu at the top right, and from the footer under every page. Its administrators sign in with their account here; there is no separate BHW Connect password any more.
Creating an API key now asks for your account’s password every time.

title: Compare two versions of a form

items.text: Compare any two versions of a form. On the form’s page, Versions → Compare shows what a version changed since the one before it, and Compare with live on the draft shows what publishing will change. You can pick any two versions at the top of the page.

Each question that changed lists every setting before and after, and added, removed and moved questions are listed too. A change that makes answers hard to compare across versions is marked: a new question type, a question made required, or a removed question. So is a change to who is asked, or to which answers a question’s text shows.
The Versions panel’s “What changed” now lists a question as changed when any of its settings changed, such as its choices or rules, not only its label, type or Required.

title: A history of each question’s changes

items.text: Every question now keeps a history: select it, then History in the right panel. It lists each change saved from this update on — who made it, when, which setting, and what it was before and after.

Put back returns a change to how it was. It first shows each setting now and after, then saves it like any edit, so Undo reverses it. A change of type or a move is listed but not put back — change the type or drag the question instead.

title: Signatures, and what each question type can do

items.text: A Signature question can now be answered: people sign with a finger, a pen or the mouse, on the web form and in manual entry. The signature shows on the response page and in the response PDF.

Help → Builder reference → What each type can do: a table of every question type and where it works — the builder, the web form, manual entry, paper and scan, the PDF, spreadsheets, Google Sheets and Airtable, analytics and conditions.
The “Adv” mark in the question list now says what it means: the type works like any other, and its settings are more technical.
A photo, file or signature in a spreadsheet export now has a link to open it; you sign in to open it.

title: Philippine places, and choices narrowed by another form

items.text: A Cascading select can use the Philippine Standard Geographic Code (PSGC) from the Philippine Statistics Authority: Levels tab → Philippine places (PSGC). It gives Region, Province or district, City or municipality, and Barangay, from the 3Q 2026 list. When a level has only one choice, such as a city outside any province, it fills itself in.

Show only the choices another form has answers for — for example, only the barangays with a report in another form — or only those with none yet. Set it with Show only, on a cascade level or on a question whose choices come from a list file or another form.
Manual entry opens faster for forms with long choice lists: the lists now load beside the page.

title: Grids from lists, and sections as tables

items.text: A Grid's or Likert matrix's rows can come from a list file or another form's answers: Grid tab → Rows come from. A grid column's choices can too. They are copied in when you publish; publish again to pick up new answers.
Add and rename a grid's rows and columns right in the builder's Preview.

A repeatable section can be laid out as a table: each question is a column and each entry a row, with Add row and Remove row. Phones still show one card per entry. Section → Advanced → Layout → Table.
The response PDF and the paper form draw a table section as a table.

title: Choices from lists and other forms

items.text: Multiple choice questions can take their choices from another form's answers, as Single choice and Dropdown already could.
Upload a list as a CSV or Excel file and use it for a Single choice, Multiple choice or Dropdown question: Options → Choices come from → A list file.
Short text questions can suggest answers as people type, from a list file or another form's answers. Any other answer is still accepted.
The builder's Preview shows choices from a list file or another form. A long list shows its first 200.
Excel turns a code like 01 into 1. The upload now says how to keep codes as text.

title: Grids that work like tables

items.text: Grids: give each column its own type (one choice, several choices, text, a number or a date) and its own list of choices.
Grids and Likert matrices are drawn as tables on computers and tablets, and as cards on phones.
A Likert scale is drawn as one line of points with the words underneath.
Spreadsheets, Google Sheets and Airtable get a column for every grid cell, beside the usual summary column.
The printed form shows each grid cell's choices as tick boxes, and a writing box for text, numbers and dates.

title: Small fixes for a tidier, more consistent look

items.text: Error messages are easier to read in dark mode, in one shade of red everywhere, including the forms people fill in.
Dialogs space their paragraphs evenly, such as Move scope and Delete scope.
Point at a cut-off name, web address or reply to read it in full.

title: Version numbers, What's new, and the testing rounds so far

items.text: Version number in the sidebar, under every page and on the sign-in page.
What's new opens after you sign in when something changed; always one click away at the foot of every page.
Feedback: tag a report as a bug, a suggestion or a question, and follow every testing-round comment under Feedback & testing.
The builder: insert a question into a formula or a label, use another question's answer as a limit, and build a calculation from presets such as Age and Join answers.
Default values fill in when a form opens, and Today follows the form's time zone.
